locations.paragraph: Instant checking~\cite{instant}, dynamic constraints~\cite{dynamic}, and incremental handling of complex rules~\cite{complex} directly overlap dependency-based invalidation, including finer rule parts. Work on incremental builds addresses dependency validity~\cite{pluto}; the Build Systems \`a la Carte framework separates scheduling and rebuilding~\cite{alacarte}. More general models include imperative self-adjusting computation~\cite{imperative}, Adapton~\cite{adapton}, Differential Dataflow~\cite{differential}, and Rete~\cite{rete}. Falleri et al. reduce memory through statically derived, pre-instantiated impact lists rather than a model-sized read cache~\cite{lowmemory}. The measured comparison is among our representations, not an executed performance comparison with these general consistency systems.

Assume an owned immutable snapshot during evaluation; deterministic, read-only owner predicates; complete mediation of all observations, including missing lookups, iteration and membership; a complete normalized transaction; and correct maintenance of $U$ and $G$. An unaffected old owner has equal values for every observation in its old execution trace. If its new execution first diverged, the observation causing that first divergence would be one reached on the identical prefix, hence in the old trace, contradicting Equation~\ref{eq:invalidate}. Its output can therefore be reused. Changed/new owners are evaluated on $F'$, removed owners are discarded, and the union equals reevaluation of $q$ on all new owners. This is an instance of established dependency reasoning, not a new general soundness theorem~\cite{dynamic,complex,pluto}.

A configured origin map associates public-looking origins with local directories. HTTP status and Location are interpreted together~\cite{http}; a Location field on a 201 response is not treated as a redirect. URI handling resolves references, lowercases scheme/authority, and removes fragments while retaining path case, query strings, and slash distinctions~\cite{uri}. locations.paragraph: We distinguish Web representation semantics, discovery-service conventions, and application release policy. HTML's language and alternate-link semantics~\cite{htmllang,htmlalternate} do not imply that every content item must exist in every locale. Language declaration also serves accessibility and processing purposes beyond search~\cite{w3clang}. BCP~47 defines language tags and a separate specification defines matching~\cite{bcp47,langmatch}; our implementation normalizes tag case but does not claim complete registry validation or general language-range negotiation.

locations.paragraph: The HTTP Link reader respects delimiters inside quoted values. It retains repeated \texttt{hreflang} parameters; only the first \texttt{rel} parameter is used. Since the profile does not implement an alternate anchor context, it ignores the entire anchored link rather than attaching it to the response resource~\cite{weblinking}. Duplicate JSON members and normalized route collisions are rejected. Local paths must remain inside their mounted directories. XML parsing rejects DTD/entity declarations and malformed input; it does not fetch external sitemap indexes. An optional Chromium adapter supplies a separately implemented HTML tree path. It parses local strings through inert \texttt{DOMParser}, whose scripts are not evaluated~\cite{domparser}, then selects active HTML-namespace metadata and anchors. Resource requests are blocked, input is never navigated, and a script sentinel remains unset. The response URL is supplied explicitly because the parser's document URL belongs to its surrounding context. Both paths use the same URL normalizer; the comparison therefore isolates tree construction and selection, not URL-standard conformance. Scripting-dependent \texttt{noscript} content remains diagnostic.

A permitted cross-locale target or fallback expresses release policy, not a proof of content duplication, translation quality or search-engine acceptance.

Accordingly, a contract selects channels rather than requiring all three. A chosen channel can advertise a deliberate subset, omit optional \texttt{x-default}, or permit fallback. Reciprocal checking applies only where that contract enables it. Sitemap membership and optional channel agreement are separate obligations, informed by the sitemap format and publication guidance~\cite{sitemaps,googlesitemap}. The checker does not turn every recommendation into a mandatory Web-standard rule.

locations.paragraph: We distinguish Web representation semantics, discovery-service conventions, and application release policy. HTML's language and alternate-link semantics~\cite{htmllang,htmlalternate} do not imply that every content item must exist in every locale. Language declaration also serves accessibility and processing purposes beyond search~\cite{w3clang}. BCP~47 defines language tags and a separate specification defines matching~\cite{bcp47,langmatch}; our implementation normalizes tag case but does not claim complete registry validation or general language-range negotiation.

Crawl Cove provides page and sitemap hreflang checks~\cite{crawlcove}. We execute its pinned page API, retaining its error/warning distinction, and compare only interpretable cohorts. Our route, reachability, HTML-only, and joint-output controls are explicitly authored scope controls. The comparison isolates whether a checker receives independent content identities, rather than treating additional contract information as superior link analysis.

For an external comparison, we retain Crawl Cove 1.0.0's full source at a pinned commit and its MIT license~\cite{crawlcove}. The unavailable XML dependency is removed together with sitemap-only initialization and functions; the page-checking functions are unchanged. A reproducible preparation script records this transformation. The page API receives an injected local-response fetch function; global network fetch is disabled. Each relevant local page is supplied with its recorded HTML, status, and headers, and the alternate limit is raised to avoid truncation. We executed \ExternalPages{} page calls and \ExternalFetches{} local fetches over the primary release candidates. This is dependency-pruned page-API execution, not installation of the full CLI, sitemap mode, or desktop product.

The revised parser implements an explicit static profile on Python's event parser~\cite{htmlparser}, not a browser engine. It requires an explicit head, ignores inert template content~\cite{htmltemplate}, and declines constructs needing unsupported recovery or foreign-content interpretation. A first active base element governs HTML references~\cite{htmlbase}, whereas relative HTTP Link targets use the response URL. locations.paragraph: A further pipeline executes Pandoc 3.1.11.1, using its Markdown reader, HTML writer, template and metadata facilities~\cite{pandoc}. Five complete Markdown sources from the same pinned Polyglot repository are retained without body edits: the English about page and four language versions of a custom-permalink example. Pandoc reads source metadata; a separately retained source-index record defines the contract. The authored header/template integration passes the source-derived content key, language, canonical, and alternate links to the compiler. The \PandocReleases{} releases require \PandocCalls{} native HTML compilation calls plus five metadata-reader calls. Ordinary body-link checking is disabled because these five excerpts do not include the entire site's target universe. Jekyll Liquid is not executed. This is an authored Pandoc publication pipeline over public sources, not rebuilding the upstream Jekyll site or adding an independent source repository.

locations.paragraph: The HTTP Link reader respects delimiters inside quoted values. It retains repeated \texttt{hreflang} parameters; only the first \texttt{rel} parameter is used. Since the profile does not implement an alternate anchor context, it ignores the entire anchored link rather than attaching it to the response resource~\cite{weblinking}. Duplicate JSON members and normalized route collisions are rejected. Local paths must remain inside their mounted directories. XML parsing rejects DTD/entity declarations and malformed input; it does not fetch external sitemap indexes. An optional Chromium adapter supplies a separately implemented HTML tree path. It parses local strings through inert \texttt{DOMParser}, whose scripts are not evaluated~\cite{domparser}, then selects active HTML-namespace metadata and anchors. Resource requests are blocked, input is never navigated, and a script sentinel remains unset. The response URL is supplied explicitly because the parser's document URL belongs to its surrounding context. Both paths use the same URL normalizer; the comparison therefore isolates tree construction and selection, not URL-standard conformance. Scripting-dependent \texttt{noscript} content remains diagnostic.

entries.title: Incremental inconsistency detection with low memory overhead

locations.paragraph: Instant checking~\cite{instant}, dynamic constraints~\cite{dynamic}, and incremental handling of complex rules~\cite{complex} directly overlap dependency-based invalidation, including finer rule parts. Work on incremental builds addresses dependency validity~\cite{pluto}; the Build Systems \`a la Carte framework separates scheduling and rebuilding~\cite{alacarte}. More general models include imperative self-adjusting computation~\cite{imperative}, Adapton~\cite{adapton}, Differential Dataflow~\cite{differential}, and Rete~\cite{rete}. Falleri et al. reduce memory through statically derived, pre-instantiated impact lists rather than a model-sized read cache~\cite{lowmemory}. We instead retain the exact dynamic read set and factor repeated owner/fact footprints. This preserves the field index's invalidation set but remains data-dependent in space. The measured comparison is among our representations, not an executed performance comparison with these general consistency systems.
